description: Per-isotope diagnostic correlating B_E (or mass) error against inter-nucleon channel counts (pp / pn / nn) and the signed h-weight sum.  Tests whether the +2.89 % residual is uniform (PR #1063 single-knot VolDensity refinement framing) or whether channel-assignment effects drive sign-flips across the low-isotope sequence.  KLR-positivity (observables ≥ 0) is checked separately; sign-flips in PREDICTION error are not a KLR violation per se (the underlying tr_M values remain positive) but they DO indicate weighting miscalibration.

parameters.channel_d_coefficients: pp:0, pn:-h/2, nn:-h (per isotope_record_schema.py CrossingType: SIGMA=(1,0), AVERAGED=(1,-h/2), SIGMA_INV=(1,-h))

prediction_error_sign_flips.interpretation: OVER-prediction (err > 0) → extra positive contributions OR under-weighted negative channels
OVER-prediction (err > 0) → extra positive contributions OR under-weighted negative channels
OVER-prediction (err > 0) → extra positive contributions OR under-weighted negative channels
UNDER-prediction (err < 0) → missing positive contributions OR over-weighted negative channels

data.verdict: STRONG correlation between err_pct and inter-nucleon channel counts/weights — the per-isotope error is dominated by the channel-assignment layer, NOT by a single-knot VolDensity(𝓑₃) refinement.  This FALSIFIES the PR #1063 framing for the low-isotope cluster.  R&D should redirect to the categorical backing of the pp/pn/nn channel assignment (no `prop:` block currently formalises the rule).

caveats: This diagnostic is purely empirical/statistical — it correlates observed prediction error against structural channel counts to surface miscalibration patterns.  It does NOT introduce any new calibration or fit.  A high R² indicates WHERE the miscalibration lives (channel weights vs VolDensity refinement); the FIX must still come from a categorical derivation, not from this regression.
